title: Eight killed and others missing after ferry capsizes off northern Cyprus
description: At least eight people have died and more than a dozen others are still missing after a passenger boat capsized off northern Cyprus, the head of the Tu
body: At least eight people have died and more than a dozen others are still missing after a passenger boat capsized off northern Cyprus, the head of the Turkish administration there has said.Ünal Üstel, prime minister of the self-proclaimed Turkish republic on Cyprus, said the ferry had been carrying 259 passengers and eight crew members when it began taking on water after departing the coastal town of Kyrenia.The ship's captain and seven crew members have been detained as part of an investigation into "how this tragedy occurred", Üstel wrote on social media. A search and rescue operation to find the passengers still unaccounted for is under way, which Turkish authorities have joined. The privately owned ferry left the left the popular holiday resort of Kyrenia at about 12:30 local time (09:30 GMT).Üstel said the boat had been scheduled to travel to Turkey on Saturday, but had been delayed due to poor weather conditions.He told Turkish media outlet TRT that the boat was hit by two waves before it capsized. While the captain of the vessel was trying to recover from the first wave, a second wave hit and it began taking on water, he told the outlet.Helicopters and coastguard boats have been dispatched to the scene, while ambulances have been stationed on the beach ready to receive rescued passengers.Üstel wrote on social media that the "priority right now is human life", adding that security forces, rescue teams and health officials were all on the scene.He added the disaster will be thoroughly investigated and "even the slightest negligence will be uncovered". "No one will be spared, regardless of who they are, who is found to be at fault or responsible," Üstel said.Erhan Arikli, the transport minister of the self-declared Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC), which is only recognised by Turkey, told local media that 100 passengers had been taken to shore.Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan sent his condolences to Turkish Cypriots and said efforts to reach those who were still missing "continue uninterrupted"."Immediately after the accident, we launched extensive search-and-rescue operations in co-operation with the authorities of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus," he said at a military ceremony on Sunday.Mustafa Koc saved around 65 people with his boat after the vessel capsized. He told the BBC that he felt the crew should have waited until the sea was calm."It wasn't safe for them," he said. "The sea was quite choppy."Koc added: "People died. It's not right."He said the boat had arrived in Kyrenia on Saturday and "had some damage in the front".The ferry - a high-speed 40m long, 10m wide Filo Jet vessel - sails under the flag of Turkey, according to Marine Traffic.On Sunday evening, Arikli told TRT the ship had completely sunk.Filo Denizcilik, the company which operates the capsized passenger boat, said it was "deeply saddened by the tragic accident".A hotline has been set up to provide passengers' relatives with information. The nationalities of those who were aboard and the status of the injured are unclear.Local television has broadcast images of the upside-down ferry in the water, with people wearing life vests atop its hull.The TRNC, which is recognised only by Turkey, controls the northern third of the island of Cyprus, which has been divided since 1974.Additional reporting by Sherie Ryder

title: Joe Root: England captain calm on form, saying 'I've got 14,000 runs for a reason'
description: Joe Root is "not too concerned" about his recent modest returns with the bat, saying he has "14,000 runs for a reason".Captain Root, England's all-tim
body: Joe Root is "not too concerned" about his recent modest returns with the bat, saying he has "14,000 runs for a reason".Captain Root, England's all-time leading Test run-scorer, has passed 50 only twice this summer. An average of 29.44 is his second-lowest in a home season in a 14-year international career.The 35-year-old has been lbw nine times in his past seven Tests, including on seven occasions this summer.But Root pointed to the challenge faced by all batters against the moving ball in the UK this summer and his own remarkable Test career. Only India great Sachin Tendulkar has more than the Yorkshireman's 14,208 runs."I've played this game a long time and I've always found ways of solving those problems and working it through," Root told the BBC's Today at the Test. "I don't see this as being any different."There's a reason why I've got 14,000 runs and a reason why I've played the best part of 15 years at this level."Of course it's frustrating that there's sort of a trend. There are probably four umpires' calls within that, which could have gone the other way, and the ball is probably deviating more than it ever has."You try and be realistic and understand where everything's at, but also be aware of what you need to do to keep improving and keep getting better. I'm pretty sure I'll get through the other side. I'm not too concerned about that."Last summer, former Australia opener David Warner took a dig at Root's prospects of success in the Ashes series that was to follow when he said: "He will have to take the surfboard off his front leg."At the time, Warner's suggestion Root had an lbw problem was incorrect. In a run that began in August 2022 and ended with the fourth Ashes Test in Melbourne in December, Root was lbw to seam bowlers in Test cricket on only three occasions.However, Root's recent run of leg-before dismissals began when he was trapped by Australia's Jhye Richardson in the second innings of the Boxing Day Test. Since then he has been lbw nine times in 12 innings, all to pace bowlers.Root's specific problem has been against right-arm bowlers, pitching the ball outside off stump and nipping it back towards him.Of the nine dismissals in his run of lbws, none have come at the hands of bowlers with high pace, rather those with a maximum speed of around 84mph."You're never given anything in this game," said Root. "You have to work for everything. You have to keep working hard and I'll certainly keep doing that."You're constantly going to get challenged and you're constantly going to have to look to evolve and learn, but that's never been something I've shied away from and I certainly won't be doing moving forward."Root not only highlighted the difficulty of conditions, but also suggested batting is being made harder by what he perceived to be a different technique employed by ball manufacturers Dukes."The balls have been different this summer," he said. "I think there is a different lacquer. They were worried about it going out of shape. They are denting surfaces more."When contacted by the BBC, Dukes denied any alteration to its process.Root was backed to solve the lbw issue by former England captain Michael Vaughan, who said: "He's always overcome problems and I'm pretty sure he'll overcome this one."It is an issue because it's happening on a regular basis, but he's had issues in the past that he's managed to come back from. There's no question he'll be fine in time."Despite there being no big contribution from the captain, England secured a series win over Pakistan with a 194-run win in the second Test at Lord's.It gave Root a second win in as many matches at the beginning of his second spell as skipper, and England their first series victory since 2024.The build-up to the second Test was dominated by the controversy surrounding England pace bowler Brydon Carse, who was dropped from the squad because of an incident outside a nightclub in Derby.On Tuesday, Root said he was "hacked off" to be dealing with another drinking issue involving an England player and confirmed he had addressed his squad to warn them against a repeat.On Sunday, Root said he wanted his players to celebrate the win at Lord's "sensibly"."It's important that we're not talking about that, absolutely," said Root. "It's hard to win Test matches, it's hard to win Test series."Enjoy it and celebrate it, but in a sensible and grown-up way."Vaughan suggested the England squad should "stay in"."Have a quiet one," Vaughan said. "I don't want to be picking up the paper tomorrow morning or mid-afternoon on social media and seeing a few clicks. You've won a good series, just have a quiet night."

schema.headline: Joe Root: England captain calm on form, saying 'I've got 14,000 runs for a reason'

title: Head teacher evacuated 900 children minutes before Nepal floods hit
description: The warnings had come from four different people in the space of minutes and helped him evaluate the impending danger."A parent came and told me that
body: The warnings had come from four different people in the space of minutes and helped him evaluate the impending danger."A parent came and told me that 'a big flood was coming, I am here to take my daughter, I will take her'," he added."Parents don't rush without a strong reason, so it was confirmed that I shouldn't waste a second to evacuate the children."I decided I shouldn't delay any more. Even if the flood was not coming, it was just a matter of a single day's classes."I feel proud that we saved so many lives."The floods - which decimated parts of Nepal on Wednesday and have left at least 2,426 people missing - saw the school building buried under mud and debris.Dawadi said the waters arrived so quickly that a hostel building about 100m (328ft) from the river was engulfed immediately.At first, many students did not realise how serious the situation was.Pupil Yunisha Amatya, 16, said she scrambled to safety with her friends just before the flood hit."I along with my friends survived by just 10 seconds only," she told the BBC."Just before the flood came, we were in the class studying. Teachers had gathered in one place and initially had no idea what had happened. After five minutes teachers came and informed us about the flood and asked us to go home."She said one student fainted after hearing about the disaster, but many initially underestimated the danger and waited for classmates who were in a maths lesson.Yunisha and her friends scrambled uphill through an escape route behind the school."I could not walk fast, and my friends helped me to climb uphill. We tried our best to be in the safer zones then. We escaped through a narrow ladder from backside of the school. Within no time, the bazaar was swept away in front of my eyes," she says, referring to the local market around the school."If there was no grip in my shoes I would have fallen and students and other people were jostling each other to reach the safer area while escaping. The people who choose to escape from another route are apparently swept away."Students and teachers initially moved a few hundred metres uphill to safety before making their way to a neighbouring village.With roads cut off and transport disrupted, many remained stranded for two nights before rescue efforts reached them.The principal and Yunisha, who both live across the river from the school, were eventually airlifted back to their home village.Meanwhile parents were desperately trying to contact their children and relatives.Yunisha's mother, Sabina Kumari Shrestha, says she repeatedly tried to call both her daughter and husband, but neither could be reached.Her husband, Yubaraj Amatya, immediately headed towards the school."Soon after the flood news spread, I tried my daughter's number, but she was not reachable, then I was afraid," he said."Within a few minutes I rushed toward my daughter's school and Trishuli Bazar was all swept by the flood, then I thought my daughter was no more. I was so horrified, stopped my scooter, there was flooding but I could not think of returning without my daughter."For nearly an hour, he had no idea whether she was alive and kept calling her without success. Then the phone finally connected and Yunisha answered."Finally, my daughter received my call and I couldn't stop myself, broke out... two relatives that were with me also cried and hugged me," he said.Yunisha appears tearful as she recalls that moment."After I had reached the top of the hill, I received a call from my father. He was tearful and I could not speak a word then," she said.Back home, her family waited anxiously for her return."Even my younger daughter couldn't sleep. But I felt so good to see her after three days (Friday), I am so happy and relieved," her mother said.Yunisha says she is now thinking about what comes next."Now I am worried about my further studies," she said."If I had to change my school, I would have to miss my old friends and will face difficulties to make new friends. I am sad about my further studies."Head teacher Dawadi says better warning systems, including sirens and evacuation alerts, could have helped residents respond sooner.But he believes his decision to act immediately prevented a catastrophe."Had I decided to close the school after the period, nothing might be left, only the bell would be ringing at 9:30."

schema.headline: Head teacher evacuated 900 children minutes before Nepal floods hit

title: Switzerland rave shooting kills woman, 22 as manhunt launched
description: A manhunt is under way after a 22-year-old woman was killed and five others injured in a shooting at a rave in Switzerland.Italian national Maria Spin
body: A manhunt is under way after a 22-year-old woman was killed and five others injured in a shooting at a rave in Switzerland.Italian national Maria Spinelli died at the scene in Aarau on Sunday morning, police said. Four men and a woman, aged between 24 and 27, were in hospital with injuries "ranging from minor to severe".Italy's prime minister Giorgia Meloni said she was confident Swiss authorities would "shed full light on what happened and find anyone responsible".Aarau cantonal police spokesman Michael Leupold told a news conference on Sunday afternoon that officers were "still in the midst of the operation" and had no leads on who may have been behind the shooting.Organisers and performers said the shooting happened at a techno rave being held at a horse racing track in the town, which is located some 46km (29 miles) west of Zurich.The force said it had received an initial report of shots fired at the Schachen race track at around 02:30 local time (00:30 GMT).Leupold reiterated that the police were conducting a large-scale, nationwide manhunt for the perpetrator, but said that there were currently no leads on whether it was one person or multiple individuals.They were not believed to be in Aarau anymore, he added.The investigation is being carried out in co-operation with Freiburg police, German news agency DPA reported.Italy's foreign ministry said in a statement that it was sending officials to Zurich "to closely follow the investigation".It added that two other Italians "were slightly injured and have already returned home".The Italian Embassy in Bern and the Consulate in Zurich were monitoring the situation, they said. A DJ, who was due to perform until the scheduled end of the event at 02:00, said the incident occurred "straight after our set", in a post on social media.Another performer, DJ Tekibo, said he had lost a friend in the incident. He wrote on Instagram that he was "still trying to process what happened".Olivier Grein, whose firm Agency Events AG organised the event, said the company was "shaken" and would do all it could to support the police investigation.An eyewitness told Blick that he "suddenly heard the gunshots" minutes after the music stopped at 02:30, initially believing they were fireworks.He said he was told to hide by a man and a woman, the latter of whom was then shot.Organisers had expected up to 3,500 people to attend. Police asked witnesses to submit photographs and video from the scene.An area around the racing track, the town's swimming pool and sports field has been cordoned off, with the public urged to stay away.A large contingent of officers has also been deployed beyond Aarau "as a precaution", the cantonal police said. An AFP journalist reported seeing armed officers deployed on the highway up to 30km from the site of the shooting.Aarau, home to approximately 23,000 people, is less than 40km from the border with Germany, where local media reported police were supporting Swiss forces.

schema.headline: Switzerland rave shooting kills woman, 22 as manhunt launched

title: Woman injured in fatal police pursuit crash near Stratford-upon-Avon dies
description: A woman who was critically injured when her car was in collision with a vehicle involved in a police pursuit has died.The 62-year-old was the driver o
body: A woman who was critically injured when her car was in collision with a vehicle involved in a police pursuit has died.The 62-year-old was the driver of a Ford Puma which collided with an Audi A3 on the A439 Warwick Road near Stratford-upon-Avon in Warwickshire on Monday.The driver of the Audi, a 19-year-old man, died at the scene. The Audi was being followed by police officers after it had earlier failed to pull over when requested to do so.The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) has begun an investigation and said thoughts were with the friends and families of both those who died. The families have requested privacy, a statement said."We can confirm that a woman who was critically injured in a road traffic incident in Warwick Road, Stratford-upon-Avon on Monday (24 Aug) has, sadly, died," the statement said."The 62-year-old woman's Ford Puma was in collision with a black Audi A3 car which had been pursued by officers from Warwickshire Police."The Audi driver died at the scene."Our thoughts are with the friends and families of both those who have died and both families have requested privacy at this difficult time."Warwickshire Police was also contacted for a comment, but said it was directing inquiries to the IOPC. It has referred the crash to the police complaints watchdog because a death had occurred following police contact.Police previously said the pursuit began shortly before 17:30 BST on Birmingham Road when officers attempted to stop the Audi, but the driver failed to pull over.The crash happened about 15 minutes later, the force said.The Ford driver, initially reported to be in her 70s, was taken to hospital along with another woman, who had been a passenger in the Ford.West Midlands Ambulance Service said the second woman had suffered serious injuries, but they were not thought to be life threatening.Injuries to another patient from the Ford were not believed to be serious.After failing to stop, the Audi made off in the direction of the A46 before travelling back towards Stratford on the A439.A number of other cars were damaged during the pursuit, police said.Warwick Road was closed on Monday from the Marraway roundabout to its junction with Ingon Lane and Sand Barn Lane, with the stretch remaining shut on Tuesday morning.Manuela Perteghella, Liberal Democrat MP for Stratford-on-Avon, said on Tuesday the incdent was "incredibly tragic"."My thoughts are with the families of all those impacted. We must now let the investigation take its course."The IOPC is asking anyone who may have footage of the Audi or the pursuit to contact them.

schema.headline: Woman injured in fatal police pursuit crash near Stratford-upon-Avon dies

title: Lake Ontario sign installed in Canada in latest jab at US
description: Figure caption, Watch: Ontario Premier Doug Ford unveils 'Lake Ontario' signByYang TianUpdated 7 hours agoOntario Premier Doug Ford has hit back at Do
body: Figure caption, Watch: Ontario Premier Doug Ford unveils 'Lake Ontario' signByYang TianUpdated 7 hours agoOntario Premier Doug Ford has hit back at Donald Trump by installing a large sign on Canada's shoreline with the message: "Lake Ontario. Now and Always."The US president signed an executive order on Thursday seeking to change its name to Lake America and has shared a series of AI-generated videos about the lake that straddles both countries."Long before President Trump, this lake was called Lake Ontario. Long after President Trump is gone, it will still be called Lake Ontario," Ford said.The war of words was triggered after trade talks collapsed, with the US imposing new 50% tariffs on $20bn (C$28bn) of Canadian goods. Canada will implement "dollar for dollar" counter-tariffs next month.Figure caption, Watch: "He's losing it" - Americans react to Lake Ontario name changeTrump said the decree was effective immediately as he signed the order to rename it Lake America. While he has broad discretion over how the US recognises landmarks, other countries are not required to follow. On Saturday, Google said it had changed the name on its maps for users in the US."Since we update Google Maps to reflect name changes in official government sources, which is GNIS [Geographic Names Information System] for the US, people using Maps in the US will see 'Lake America', those in Canada will continue to see 'Lake Ontario' and those outside of the US and Canada will see both names," the tech firm said in a blog post.This mirrors how Google names the Gulf of Mexico for users after Trump declared it was called the Gulf of America in 2025.Image source, Google MapsImage caption, Google Maps now displays the lake as Lake America in the USCanadian officials have dismissed Trump's move.On Saturday, Trump also posted several AI-generated videos on social media, with one showing him kicking over a Lake Ontario sign and replacing it with one that says: "Welcome to Lake America."Another video depicted a flock of Canada geese sporting the US president's trademark hair and holding rifles as they patrolled the shoreline of a newly named Lake America.Ford said Trump's renaming of the lake was because he "didn't like Ontario and Canada standing up for ourselves".Standing in front of the newly unveiled Lake Ontario sign, Ford added: "Just in case President Trump or anyone else forgets, we've set up this sign to remind them, it's Lake Ontario, now and forever."It echoes Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney's previous response to the row, insisting "things must be called by their name, and this lake is called Lake Ontario - today and forever".The names of four of the Great Lakes - Ontario, Huron, Michigan and Erie - originate from indigenous words. Lake Superior was named after an anglicised French word. Lake Ontario, the smallest of the Great Lakes, borders both the Canadian province and the US state of New York.Trump's executive order gives the US Department of the Interior 30 days to update the name change with the Geographic Names Information Service - the official repository of domestic geographic names in the US.Mexico similarly rejected Trump's renaming of the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America, arguing a single country could not rename a shared body of international water.

schema.headline: Lake Ontario sign installed in Canada in latest jab at US

title: Man killed at Big Church Festival named as his church leads tributes
description: The man killed at a Christian festival in West Sussex on Friday has been named by his church as Robert Guanco, 41.He was a pastor at Jesus the Living
body: The man killed at a Christian festival in West Sussex on Friday has been named by his church as Robert Guanco, 41.He was a pastor at Jesus the Living Water Church in Eastbourne, East Sussex.Six other people were injured at the event by a falling sign at the Big Church Festival, near Steyning, four of whom were taken to hospital for treatment.In a statement, his church said: "Pastor Robert was a faithful servant of God, a loving husband to Isay, a devoted and caring father to Ellie, and a blessing to so many people whose lives he touched. His life, his faith, his love, and his service to God will never be forgotten."On a fundraising page for Guanco's family, pastor Norman Ponce from Jesus the Living Water Worldwide Church, said he was a "faithful servant of God"."What was meant to be a time of worship, fellowship, and celebration became an unimaginable tragedy," he added.Ponce said Guanco was a "beloved son, cherished brother, loving husband" and "great father"."He was also a good friend, mentor, and a blessing to so many people whose lives he touched," Ponce said."His life reflected humility, faith, love, compassion, and service.  Through his ministry, kindness, prayers, and encouragement, he touched many lives."Eastbourne MP Josh Babarinde said earlier in the summer he met with members of the congregation of Guanco's church."Their energy and spirit was inspiring," he said."This, in so many ways, is a testament to his pastorship and his commitment to his church."I cannot imagine how difficult this must be for his family - Pastor Robert was a father and husband too - and I send them and his church my most sincere condolences."The Big Church Festival, which describes itself as the UK's biggest Christian festival, was founded in 2009.The event at Wiston Park began on Friday and was due to continue until Sunday, but a decision was made by organisers to cancel the remainder of the event after the incident.The organisers said they were "heartbroken" by Guanco's death, adding: "Big Church Festival is about bringing people together."At the moment, that community is grieving."The Archbishop of Canterbury said she was "sad and shocked" to hear about the fatal incident.Dame Sarah Mullally said: "I pray for his family, friends and loved ones as they grieve. I pray for those receiving treatment, and the healthcare workers looking after them."And I pray too for the other festival goers, staff and event organisers as they come to terms with these tragic events."Witnesses said people rushed to lift the heavy sign, which read "Everything's Unmissable", after it had fallen over in the wind.Festival organisers said they were working with emergency services as they established the circumstances surrounding the incident.Sussex Police is urging anyone with information about the incident to contact them.The force said the Health and Safety Executive and local authority had also been informed about the incident.Follow BBC Sussex on Facebook, external, X, external, and Instagram, external and listen to BBC Radio Sussex on Sounds. Send your story ideas to southeasttoday@bbc.co.uk , external or WhatsApp us on 08081 002250.

title: England vs Pakistan player ratings: Ollie Robinson stars again but is Joe Root's form a worry?
description: Ben Duckett - 4 - Another quiet Test for Duckett whose total of 18 runs across the match was only three more than at Headingley last week. Could do li
body: Ben Duckett - 4 - Another quiet Test for Duckett whose total of 18 runs across the match was only three more than at Headingley last week. Could do little about his first-innings dismissal but the way he hit a drive straight to mid-off in the second was really poor.Emilio Gay - 5 - So unlucky to be the latest victim of the poor Lord's pitch after reaching 31 in the second innings. The third Test at Edgbaston could be a big week for the opener.Jordan Cox - 7 - Very impressive again in making 55 in the first innings. As wickets fell around him, Cox remained composed. Yet to make a score that completely forces the selectors' hand but he is building a strong case to stay when Jacob Bethell is fit again.Joe Root - 5 - Scores of four and 24 as England's captain fell lbw in both innings. Seven of his nine Test dismissals this summer have been in that fashion. It is not a crisis... yet…Harry Brook - 6 - Nothing spectacular from Brook, who made 15 and 34, but he took a more restrained approach than in similar recent Tests when faced with difficult conditions.Dan Lawrence - 7 - After being dropped and then run out in making 17 in the first innings, Lawrence responded with a useful 54 in the second that suggested he does have the skills for this role, with the bat at least.Jamie Smith - 8 - His best performance for a year. Smith's 61 in difficult conditions in the first innings was perfectly played. Again, kept well up to the stumps to Ollie Robinson. His glovework has gone up a level.Gus Atkinson - 5 - The one member of England's pace quartet who is struggling for wickets. Bowled quickly on day four but still only has one scalp in the series. His 45 with the bat in the first innings was handy.Ollie Robinson - 9 - This is turning into Ollie Robinson's summer. After another eight wickets, England's seamer now has 23 wickets in three Tests at an average of 8.34 since his recall. Jofra Archer - 8 - Brilliant in the first innings when he was unfortunate to finish with just the three wickets. His bouncer to dismiss Babar Azam on day four was a throwback of Archer's fearsome debut on the same ground.Josh Tongue - 7 - Pakistan did not recover after Tongue took the key wickets of Babar Azam and Abdullah Shafique in the first innings. Also improved his Test high score to 30 not out.Shan Masood - 5 - Battled in the second innings for 26 but only made one in the first.Azan Awais - 6 - Rode his luck against Archer but otherwise played nicely for 46 in the first innings before being Robinson'd in the second.Abdullah Shafique - 2 - Five in the first innings, a duck in the second. Shafique was Pakistan's best batter in the first Test but went missing here.Imam-ul-Haq - 1 - Didn't bat, didn't bowl, dropped a catch. Babar Azam - 2 - Best thing he did was win the toss.Saud Shakeel - 7- Finally a bit of fight from Pakistan. Deserved his century. Muhammad Rizwan - 5 - A mark boosted by his admirable keeping up to the stumps.Ali Usman - 4 - These were not conditions for a spinner so hard to judge fairly. He is not a Test number eight with the bat, never mind seven where he had to emerge here after Imam's injury.Khurram Shahzad - 3 - Just as expensive as Headingley and only took three wickets despite favourable conditions.Muhammad Abbas - 8 - Nine wickets in the match, including 5-57 in the second innings to put him on the honours board. Much improved on Headingley and a constant threat with conditions in his favour.Mohammad Ali - 6 - Also better than he was at Headingley, nipping the ball in and out, but he won't find conditions better suited to his style.

schema.headline: England vs Pakistan player ratings: Ollie Robinson stars again but is Joe Root's form a worry?

title: Seven arrested after death of newborn baby girl in Sheffield
description: Seven people have been arrested on suspicion of murder after the death of a newborn baby girl in Sheffield, police said. Officers were called at about
body: Seven people have been arrested on suspicion of murder after the death of a newborn baby girl in Sheffield, police said. Officers were called at about 06:00 BST on Sunday to a property on Holywell Heights in the Wincobank area following reports of a concern for the safety of the baby.  South Yorkshire Police said, despite the best efforts of officers and paramedics, the baby was pronounced dead at the scene.Det Ch Insp Emma Knight confirmed the force was "working to determine the ages of some of those arrested".She said: "We are aware news of this will be deeply concerning and I want to reassure our local communities that we have a dedicated team of detectives and officers hard at work to ensure justice is secured for the baby girl at the heart of this investigation."Knight added: "Our investigation is in its early stages and we would like to remind people to avoid speculating about this incident."

schema.headline: Seven arrested after death of newborn baby girl in Sheffield

title: Mum says family 'lucky to be alive' after Burscough train crash
description: Image source, Sophie CassidyImage caption, Sophie Cassidy was on the train with her children when it collided with the van ByMarc Waddington and Stewa
body: Image source, Sophie CassidyImage caption, Sophie Cassidy was on the train with her children when it collided with the van ByMarc Waddington and Stewart WhittinghamNorth WestA rail passenger has told how she feels "lucky to be alive" after her train crashed with a van, killing the delivery driver.Sophie Cassidy was travelling in the train when it hit a van on a railway line. The van driver died at the scene in Burscough, West Lancashire, just after 15:00 BST on Saturday.The 26-year-old's daughter was hit by flying glass when the door to the Northern train driver's compartment sheered off its hinges in the crash on the Wigan Wallgate-Southport train.The mother-of-two told the BBC: "I can't put into words how lucky we are to be alive. I'm still trying to wrap my mind around it all."Image caption, British Transport Police said a man who was travelling in a van died in the crashThe marketing boss was on the train with her son and daughter.Cassidy said she had looked out through the window and saw the van travelling along a road toward the crossing just before the impact, which happened on the corner of Martin Lane and Whitehouse Lane. She described the train driver, who quickly came out of his carriage to check on all the passengers, as "an absolute hero"."The driver came out and spoke to us all and made sure we were all OK," she added.Image caption, A large emergency services presence was on the scene close to the railway line in BurscoughAll the passengers had to remain on the train for at least two hours until they could be led to safety.Cassidy said: "The fire service got us all down one by one. All the emergency services were offering us counselling."She had she had been "very tearful" since the incident, thinking about the driver who lost his life.Two people were treated for injuries at the scene.Cassidy added her daughter‘s injuries from the glass was thankfully “just a surface wound”.A British Transport Police (BTP) spokesman said: "Enquiries are ongoing to establish the full circumstances of what happened."Get in touchTell us which stories we should cover in Lancashire

schema.headline: Mum says family 'lucky to be alive' after Burscough train crash

title: Iceland votes against restarting EU membership talks
description: Iceland has voted against resuming talks on joining the European Union 13 years after they were broken off.Public broadcaster RUV reported that 52.8%
body: Iceland has voted against resuming talks on joining the European Union 13 years after they were broken off.Public broadcaster RUV reported that 52.8% of the more than 225,000 people who voted had rejected the government's proposal, while 47.2% had backed it. Some 12,600 votes separated them.Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir's centre-left government promised to hold a referendum by 2027, but brought it forward because of international tensions, including US President Donald Trump's threats against Greenland.However, debate in this island nation of almost 400,000 people centred more on its fishing industry rather than security concerns.With some 270,000 people eligible to vote, RUV reported the turnout of 82.5% was the highest in any Icelandic election since 2009.Already part of the EU's single market and Schengen border-free zone, full EU membership would bring Iceland into the customs union and eventually the eurozone currency union.Iceland began its application to join the EU in 2009 in the aftermath of the 2008 financial crisis and the collapse of Iceland's banking system.Its application was already well advanced when a eurosceptic government came to power in 2013 and put those talks on hold. Fishing rights were the biggest obstacle to Icelandic accession then - as they remain today.Iceland fought successfully to protect its fisheries from foreign fishermen during the Cod Wars with the UK in the 1970s - shortly after gaining independence from Denmark - and the country's fish and marine industries still account for almost 40% of its exports.Many No voters feared EU membership would mean ceding some control of these lucrative fishing grounds under the bloc's policies, which control how much a member state can catch."The No side was much more skillful in sort of tapping into the political national identity in Iceland, which emphasises formal independence, coming out of a long independence struggle coming out of Denmark," Eirikur Bergmann, a professor of politics at Bifröst University, told the BBC."And so they were able to appeal to people's very fundamental feelings."On the other hand, the Yes campaign "ran an overtly technical campaign, never really explaining the purpose or the passion in why Iceland join the EU", he said.The referendum campaign fuelled debate about Iceland's place in the world, Kristrún said after casting her ballot in the capital on Saturday.She told a news conference on Sunday afternoon that the issue of EU membership would not be revisited while her government was in office.One of her ministers denied that the result had been a setback for the government, pointing to the high turnout for the vote.There was a significant geographical divide in which way people voted, with the capital, Reykjavík, backing EU accession talks and rural areas being more in against them.The question on the ballot was: "Should Iceland resume accession negotiations with the European Union?"A Yes vote would not have been a final decision on joining the EU, but a move towards an accession agreement, which would then have to be approved by a second referendum. Equally, the No vote does not rule out the chance of Iceland resuming talks at some point in the future.While economic concerns dominated the referendum campaigns, security issues also featured.Iceland is a founder member of Nato but has no military and relies on its allies for defence. Being a part of the EU would have granted it full access to the bloc's joint defence infrastructure. The country has backed Ukraine during Russia's full-scale invasion and officials have also been alarmed by Russia's increased maritime manoeuvres near the island.But Trump's expressed interest in subsuming another Arctic island, Greenland, into the US has raised concerns more recently.Iceland's Foreign Minister Katrín Gunnarsdóttir told Sunday's news conference that she would seek to strengthen the country's defence relations with other countries following the referendum.However, Bergmann said: "The debate was firmly domestic, it was called prior to the second term of Donald Trump, and the tumults of the world didn't really penetrate into the debate."Jacob Funk Kirkegaard, a senior fellow at the European think tank Bruegel, told RUV that the EU had failed in "selling itself" even though it "clearly would like to see itself as also a security actor, particularly in the Arctic".He said the result "will be viewed as a missed opportunity - certainly for Iceland, but also the EU".An unnamed EU diplomat appeared to agree with this assessment, telling news agency Reuters that the outcome was "a clear setback for Brussels" while noting that issues of fishing and independence had been decisive.The win for the No camp was met with applause from eurosceptics elsewhere.Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, one of the main proponents of the UK's exit from the EU, said Icelanders had voted "to keep their independence".Marine Le Pen of France's National Rally said the result pointed to an "obvious truth: membership in the European Union is not the natural horizon for every European democracy".

schema.headline: Iceland votes against restarting EU membership talks

title: Burnham gets the early prison release changes he wanted - but at what cost?
description: The prime minister's announcement that he will keep hundreds of criminals behind bars who would otherwise have been released early is one he has wante
body: The prime minister's announcement that he will keep hundreds of criminals behind bars who would otherwise have been released early is one he has wanted to make for weeks.Andy Burnham had already expanded the list of people ineligible for early release and had consistently said he wanted to go further.What is not clear is exactly what has changed to allow him to do so.Earlier this month, the Ministry of Justice warned that exempting any more prisoners risked "prisons reaching capacity and collapsing".The prime minister himself previously said he had "pushed to the very limits of what is possible to do".In his exclusive interview with BBC Breakfast, Burnham picked out the release of people on controversial indefinite sentences and the deportation of foreign criminals as measures that had made his latest intervention possible.It is understood extra capacity will also be created by immediately beginning work to create new cells in existing prisons.But none of these are short-term solutions.Ending indefinite sentences will require new legislation, meaning it could be years before space is freed up.Previous governments have struggled to quickly deport foreign offenders and there are not thought to be any new returns agreements with other countries. The case of grooming gang ringleader Shabir Ahmed, who Pakistan has resisted attempts to deport, is one example.Retrofitting prisons to create more cells is also expected to take months.People in government concede that in the short-term, Burnham will only be able to follow through on today's announcement by making prisons even more full.With the adult male prison estate already running at 98% capacity, it is a move that could worry some in the sector.But in the end, the prime minister believed he simply had to act.The extra exemptions Burnham has announced are being described within government as a "political decision".That is not surprising given the intense pressure that had built up, especially around the potential for PC Andrew Harper's killers to be released early.Burnham's inner circle are mindful that political misjudgements at the start of Sir Keir Starmer's premiership caused long-lasting damage.They believe Sir Keir never recovered from early rows over freebies and winter fuel payments, and point to a lack of major mishaps in Burnham's first six weeks in office as evidence of a more slick political operation.There was some surprise in Downing Street about how much media attention the issue of early release received over the summer.That is one reason why the prime minister's aides are relishing the new parliamentary term, when news stories come along at a faster rate and so are less likely to linger in the headlines.After the initial flip-flopping on whether the government would be able to exempt more prisoners, the mother of PC Harper told BBC Breakfast that the handling of the situation had been a "hash".Government officials working on the plans have spoken to the families of victims, who made it clear they did not want the new measures to be dripped out in leaks to the media.Instead it was decided one big announcement would be the neatest option.It had seemed likely that would come in the form of a parliamentary statement on Tuesday from the justice secretary.Instead, the prime minister decided to make the announcement himself in an interview with BBC Breakfast.It is understood Burnham was mindful of mounting speculation and wanted to give victims and the public as much certainty at the earliest possible opportunity.In doing so, he may have risked the ire of the Speaker Sir Lindsay Hoyle, who is generally disdainful of governments that make major announcements outside of Parliament.He may also have offered up ammunition to the Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch, who has already accused Burnham of being a "people pleaser" who finds it difficult to say no to people.That characterisation is likely to be tested again when more stories inevitably appear about the victims of prisoners who will still be released early.It already started on Sunday morning, when the domestic abuse commissioner said she remained "deeply concerned about the number of abusers" still set to be freed.While this is not the first time Burnham has said he has pushed the system to the limit, Whitehall sources are now adamant there will be no more additional exemptions.

schema.headline: Burnham gets the early prison release changes he wanted - but at what cost?

title: Notting Hill Carnival's 60th year celebrated on family day
description: Today is all about families and the children. And they have certainly got the memo. There are children everywhere, all ready for the fun of the day. T
body: Today is all about families and the children. And they have certainly got the memo. There are children everywhere, all ready for the fun of the day. Toddling past me is surely one of Notting Hill Carnival's youngest visitors. Triny-Savannah is just 18 months old, and is here with her mum Twinsy, all the way from Paris. "It means a lot to be here," Twinsy says. She explains that her parents used to bring her and her twin sister, and now she's carrying on the tradition with the next generation. "It's the celebration of the abolition of slaves, so it's a big day of memories," Twinsy says.  Sitting on the pavement nearby I spot eight-year-old Alex and his mum, Tiana. I soon find out it's Alex's first Carnival. He has the biggest smile on his face and a water pistol loaded with paint. "I haven't been for a long time," Tiana, from Enfield, explains, "but when I was younger I used to come religiously every year and it's nice to come back with Alex."I ask Alex how he feels about the whole morning, and he says: "I love it. It's really busy, but then it's also like we're all together at the same time, so that's great."Before the parade starts, I go in search of a snack and find a food stall tucked away from all the crowds. The man being served ahead of me, Dave, bites into his snack and he's instantly in heaven. "When I bite into this, I feel like I'm about to land in Trinidad and I'm looking out of the window at the beauty," he says, still with his eyes closed, imagining it. He's eating "doubles", a street food snack of flatbreads filled with curried chickpeas.The woman serving, Christina Bedau, asks if I want to try it. Of course I do. But, hold the extra spice please, as I'm useless with anything too hot. Christina hands me her creation, and it looks great. When I taste it, I can see what Dave means, although, I think to make it a fair comparison, I should probably fly to Trinidad just to check he's being accurate. Christina has been coming to Notting Hill Carnival with her food stall, Sweet Hand Cuisine, for the past seven years. She says she "has to come" because if she didn't, the regulars who come back every year would be "up in arms". She estimates she'll sell at least 500 doubles this weekend.The family next to me catch my eye, all kitted out in matching St Vincent's outfits. Daniel's five-year-old son Asher has already got tired legs, so he's popped him on his shoulders. It could be a long day for Daniel's shoulders.Daniel explains that his wife, Rachel, is from the Caribbean island and they have all just returned from their first family holiday there. "It's great to represent St Vincent here," Daniel says. "This is a perfect kind of event," he adds. I say goodbye to the family and realise the time. I have to head off to write about my day. I take another 50 photos, at least, on the walk back to Paddington station. I spot a poster as I leave, which says: "Fund 60 more," and asks people to donate money, to keep Carnival going. I wonder what Carnival will look like in another 60 years? Perhaps some of the children I met today will remember this big milestone for the festival, and tell their children about today, in another 60 years.Listen to the best of BBC Radio London on Sounds and follow BBC London on Facebook, external, X, external and Instagram, external. Send your story ideas to hello.bbclondon@bbc.co.uk, external

title: Bruno Fernandes: Captain still setting the standard with Man Utd hat-trick
description: To sum up, the season started pretty badly for Fernandes, who was one of many players well below par in a shock 2-0 defeat at Hull City.Matters improv
body: To sum up, the season started pretty badly for Fernandes, who was one of many players well below par in a shock 2-0 defeat at Hull City.Matters improved significantly on Tuesday, as Fernandes collected the PFA Players' Player of the Year award for his phenomenal contribution to United returning to the Champions League after a two-year absence.Last season, he totted up a Premier League record of 21 assists.Before the Ipswich game, he walked on to the pitch with the sons of PC Matthew Blades, who was tragically killed in a recent head-on collision on the A66 near Middlesbrough.Once the match began, Fernandes was largely anonymous as the home side went a goal down to Gary O'Neil's side.But, when opportunity presented itself, Fernandes stepped up.First, the 31-year-old fired home a blistering equaliser after Marcelino Nunez slipped under no pressure, presenting Matheus Cunha with a clear run at the Ipswich goal, which allowed him to set up his captain.Fernandes then kept his cool to smash home a penalty in front of the Stretford End to make it 3-1 after an hour. Bearing in mind Fernandes missed two penalties in pre-season, there must have been a sizeable amount of personal pressure on the shot.Fernandes completed his third United hat-trick seven minutes after that, although arguably all his previous efforts would have been overshadowed had he managed to find the net with an audacious 55-yard effort after Ipswich lost possession straight after the restart.Goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen was backpedalling furiously and was relieved the ball ended up on top of his net rather than in it."He means a lot," said Carrick, when asked to sum up Fernandes' contribution."I mean, he's the captain. He's been here for a good number of years now and experienced a whole load of different emotions."Times like today, when you're looking towards certain players to give us that little bit of something else, he did particularly well."At the final whistle, Fernandes' initial reaction was to talk to substitute Benjamin Sesko about a technical point around a pass he had been trying to find the striker with during injury time.Fernandes then shook hands with opposing players and the officials and was heading off to find more opponents to greet when he realised he had forgotten to collect the match ball, his hat-trick reward.He swiftly turned, asked, and referee Craig Pawson handed it over.Without his contribution, Manchester United may well not have won this game - but then, you could have said that about a lot of games over the past couple of years."Obviously it was a huge week and to end with a win at home today was massive," Fernandes told BBC Sport."I said before the game to be honest; there are certain days you feel it. It is one of those days when everything comes to you and you have to take it."I hate losing and it is difficult to be positive when you lose games. It is very difficult for me to control the emotions."At this club you want to be on top of everything."

schema.headline: Bruno Fernandes: Captain still setting the standard with Man Utd hat-trick

title: Man Utd v Ipswich player ratings: Bruno Fernandes stars in Red Devils win
description: Senne Lammens: Stood firm and came out on top as Enciso charged at him. Out of his area to control and lay off a pass to Shaw at one point. 8Diogo Dal
body: Senne Lammens: Stood firm and came out on top as Enciso charged at him. Out of his area to control and lay off a pass to Shaw at one point. 8Diogo Dalot: So close to a rare goal with a curling left-footed effort. Defensively solid. 7Harry Maguire: Reliable presence at the heart of the home defence, then got lucky with the deflection, otherwise his 'goal' might have been ruled out. 8Lisandro Martinez: Experience vital on a day when the home side might have buckled. Mistake for Ipswich's late goal. 6Luke Shaw: A difficult day for the England full-back. Struggled to deal with Fatawu. 5Kobbie Mainoo: Restored to the starting line-up and good as ever on the ball. But United's midfield struggled to cope with Ipswich running at them. 6Youri Tielemans: Still to find form in a Man Utd shirt. Went down too easily in the penalty area. Not secure defensively. 5Bryan Mbeumo: Held his wide position and threatened with crosses and short passes. Unlucky Rashford's cross was deflected as he hit the bar from close range. Got his goal at the end. 6Bruno Fernandes: Hat-trick hero. Sensational performance from the captain. Thunderous equaliser, kept his nerve with the penalty after two pre-season failures and calm third. Almost scored an outrageous fourth from halfway. 10Marcus Rashford: First league start for Man Utd since December 2024. Got on the ball often enough and ran at the visitors' defence. Almost created a goal for Mbeumo. 7Matheus Cunha: Began through the middle again and alternated with Fernandes as the furthest player forward. Decent. 7Subs:Leny Yoro (on 72, Dalot): 6Noussair Mazraoui (on 72, Shaw): 6Benjamin Sesko (on 79, Cunha): 6Patrick Dorgu (on 79, Rashford): 7Andrey Santos (on 79, Mainoo): 6Subs not used: Darlow, Zirkzee, Heaven, LaceyKjell Scherpen: Superb save to deny Dalot the opener and crucial touch to deny Mbeumo an easy finish. No chance with the equaliser. 8Dara O'Shea: Robust defensive display and did well, until Fernandes took control. 6Issa Diop: Lot of scrambling defence for the former West Ham man but coped OK for the most part and talked the Ipswich rearguard through the game. 6Jacob Greaves: Composed on the ball and held his position, not getting drawn out when Cunha dropped deep. Probably lacked a bit of class at this level. 6Leif Davis: Superb pass inside Dalot to release Maeda created one good chance for the visitors. Precise execution for his goal and might have had another. 8Marcelino Nunez: Busy, in front of defence, wants to get on ball and slot in between centre-halves. Disastrous slip at just the wrong time let Man Utd in for crucial equaliser. 6Sasa Lukic: Excellent addition to Ipswich ranks. Had the game nous to halt the home side's momentum, even at the expense of a yellow card. 7Abdul Fatawu: Skinned Shaw close to the touchline and then had the awareness to pick out a team-mate as Ipswich took the lead. Booked for a poor tackle on Mbeumo but overall really good. 7Julio Ensico: Held off Shaw and Mbeumo on length-of-field run but no reward as effort lacked power. A real threat. 8Daizan Maeda: Good early raid down the left was early sign of Ipswich intentions. Shot from angle of area threatened home goal. 7Emersonn: Tried use his size to pin Maguire and Martinez back and relished the physical tussle with the England man. 6Subs:Chuba Akpom (on 46, Emersonn): 7Exequiel Palacios (on 62, Nunez): 6Darnell Furlong (on 72, Maeda): 6Abdoul Ouattara (on 73, Lukic): 5Kasey McAteer (on 83, Fatawu): 5Subs not used: Walton, Kipre, Egeli, Clarke
